title: fix(scripts): forward-parity stale-entry messages carry no card-ending keyword
body:
Part of #9597

`scripts/check-action-forward-parity.mjs` emitted a GitHub closing keyword immediately before an interpolated issue anchor at **both** of its stale-entry ratchets, inside messages a contributor is told to quote into a pull-request body. Quoting one ends the anchor card silently, from a body whose author was being careful — GitHub's parser does no sentence parsing, so hedging the surrounding sentence buys nothing.

Repaired onto the form already landed on the sibling gates (`check-lint-coverage.mjs`, `check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs`): **the keyword becomes "can be ended"**, and **the anchor is spelled `objectui#` rather than a bare `#`**, so the reference cannot match the closing grammar at all. The instruction survives in full.

> ⚠️ **Anchors below are written unresolved, as `${meta.issue}`, exactly as the source carries them.** The resolved form of the *before* text is deliberately not reproduced in this body — that form is the defect this pull request removes.

## The two sites sit on DIFFERENT ledgers, and only one is reachable today

| site | ledger | population in this tree | reachable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| stale-`KNOWN_GAPS` ratchet | `KNOWN_GAPS` | **7 entries** (gate banner: `7 known gaps`), every one anchored on objectui#4202, which is **open** | **yes** — renders the moment one entry stops excusing anything, which is exactly the workflow that produces the quote |
| stale-`UNCHECKED_FORWARDS` ratchet | `UNCHECKED_FORWARDS` | **`{}`** (gate banner: `0 payloads exempt`) | no — dormant |

⚠️ The card and its dispatch both describe these as *two `KNOWN_GAPS` sites*. They are not: the second one is the `UNCHECKED_FORWARDS` ratchet, on its own empty table. Repaired anyway — an empty ledger is precisely why this class survived three earlier repairs.

## Rendered before / after — both messages

Rendered by driving the real `analyze()` over a throwaway tree with a seeded ledger, not by reading the template.

**Site 1 — stale `KNOWN_GAPS` entry**

Before:

```
KNOWN_GAPS entry `action:x:undoable` is no longer a gap — delete it (and close #${meta.issue} once
      its last entry is gone). Left in, it re-reserves the key for a future drop.
```

After:

```
KNOWN_GAPS entry `action:x:undoable` is no longer a gap — delete it (and objectui#424242 can be
      ended once its last entry is gone). Left in, it re-reserves the key for a future drop.
```

**Site 2 — stale `UNCHECKED_FORWARDS` entry**

Before:

```
UNCHECKED_FORWARDS entry `action:x` excuses nothing — the surface's forward literal is
      excess-property checked now, or the surface is gone. Delete it (and close #${meta.issue} once
      its last entry is gone): left in, it re-reserves the surface for a future unchecked
      literal under a reason nobody re-examined.
```

After:

```
UNCHECKED_FORWARDS entry `action:x` excuses nothing — the surface's forward literal is
      excess-property checked now, or the surface is gone. Delete it (and objectui#424242
      can be ended once its last entry is gone): left in, it re-reserves the surface for a
      future unchecked literal under a reason nobody re-examined.
```

`424242` is the harness's fixture anchor. In the *after* column it is a real rendered number, so the two columns are the same kind of reading.

## The pin RENDERS the messages, and it is shown failing

`scripts/__tests__/check-action-forward-parity-closing-keyword.test.ts` drives the real `analyze()` over a throwaway tree with a **seeded** ledger that makes each ratchet fire, and asserts on the string it actually produced. A source-text assertion cannot tell a repaired emitter from a broken one — it matches a template, and it reads identically whether or not the emitter can ever fire. The cheap source leg is kept, but only as a supplement.

Ablation on the committed tree — the emitter reverted to its pre-repair wording, per site, then restored:

| leg reverted | pin result | which legs went red |
|---|---|---|
| site 1 only | **3 failed / 2 passed**, exit 1 | KNOWN_GAPS rendered leg, the positive half, the source leg |
| site 2 only | **3 failed / 2 passed**, exit 1 | UNCHECKED_FORWARDS rendered leg, the positive half, the source leg |
| both | **4 failed / 1 passed**, exit 1 | both rendered legs, the positive half, the source leg |
| restored | **5 passed**, exit 0 | — |

Each rendered leg is individually load-bearing. After every leg the file was restored with `git checkout HEAD --`, and the restore was proved by blob hash equal to the `HEAD` blob plus an empty `git diff HEAD`, not by a return code.

The positive half (`…while both still tell the reader what to do with the anchor`) is what stops "no trigger" being satisfied by deleting the instruction outright. The control leg proves the regex can fire; it builds the resolved pre-repair form at runtime rather than writing it as a literal, so this pull request adds no card-ending trigger of its own to the tree.

## Verification

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/check-action-forward-parity-closing-keyword.test.ts` | 5 passed, exit 0 |
| `pnpm exec vitest run` on the 3 affected `scripts/__tests__` files | **57 passed**, exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:action-forward-parity` | exit 0 — `5 surfaces checked against 39 runtime-read keys from 4 consumers; 19 justified omissions, 7 known gaps, 0 payloads exempt` |
| `pnpm type-check:scripts` | exit 0; both changed files confirmed present in `--listFiles` |
| `pnpm check:new-line-citations` | exit 0 — `0 new citation(s)` |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:test-path-roots` | exit 0 |
| `eslint` on both changed files | 2 files linted, 0 errors, 0 warnings |
| governed surface | `NOT GOVERNED — 2 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched` |

Read at `096f4f4dd`. Repository-wide `pnpm lint` and the full `check:*` farm are CI's run, not duplicated here; `scripts/**` is outside the eslint population that `pnpm lint` (`turbo run lint`, per-package `eslint .`) walks, and eslint here declares no type-aware linting, so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict.

## Changeset

None, per the repo's own gate rather than a judgement call:

```
$ node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs
Compared the working tree with 1cfdff814 (merge-base with origin/main): 2 file(s) changed,
0 of them published source of a package the release covers, 0 of them a manifest whose
published contract moved, 0 under a package changesets ignores, 0 changeset(s) added.
✅  No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.
```

## Acceptance notes

Reported, **not** repaired here — this card is scope-pinned to the two sites above.

- ⚠️ **This pull request makes a sentence in `scripts/check-lint-coverage.mjs` false.** The comment above its `DEBT` ratchet says the same shape *"still stands in `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs` and `scripts/check-action-forward-parity.mjs`, which this change deliberately does not reach."* The second half is no longer true as of this commit. Left alone on purpose: that sentence sits inside the region `check-lint-coverage-closing-keyword.test.ts` slices and asserts on, so editing it is a second gate's verification surface, not this card's.
- `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` carries one more site of the same shape at its **`CLAIM_DEBT`** ratchet, with a bare `#` anchor. Its ledger holds entries, so the ratchet is reachable; its anchor card is **closed**, and deliberately so — `LEDGER_ANCHORS` records it as a standing by-name exclusion under objectui#9537's ruling. So the trigger is inert today, and would re-arm silently if that ledger is ever re-anchored to an open card. Not covered by objectui#9598's Part 1, which names only `check-type-check-coverage.mjs`.
- `scripts/check-lint-rule-coverage.mjs` has the shape in a file-header comment (`objectui#` form, which GitHub does not resolve cross-repo) rather than in emitted text. Shape-only, lowest severity of the three.
- `scripts/check-cross-repo-closer-outcome.mjs` and `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` hold many instances inside their own detector corpora. Deliberate and correct — objectui#9598 already records the second by name as an exclusion any class-wide sweep must carry.
